rationale: Covers two fix rounds: 4c21bef (round 4) and ff130d8 (round 5). CR-007 was adjudicated rather than escalated, because the user instructed the run to continue completely autonomously — the auth floor is REMOVED and recorded in spec.md as Decision 5 with the rejected alternative written down; CR-008 became moot by construction; CR-009 was adjudicated as pre-existing and moved to the deferred sidecar. Each fix round was itself reviewed. Round 4's pass (blind + edge-case over the fix-up diff, plus a full acceptance re-audit over the whole branch) found that the round-3 predicate unification made the downgrade warning fire for ordinary name reuse — both lenses convergent — and acceptance found three artifact/test-fidelity gaps; all were fixed in 4c21bef and the spec. Round 5's pass found that a displaced OAuth-bearing default was reported nowhere, again convergent across both lenses; fixed in ff130d8. Both lenses in round 5 recommended URL normalization as the underlying fix; that was considered and REJECTED for this task because it changes which entries displace which, touches AC5, and contradicts spec §5 — it is the pre-existing deferred finding, and the residual harm was reduced (not eliminated) by making displacement reportable. All 8 acceptance criteria pass. Out-of-band gate evidence at HEAD ff130d8: build exit 0, unit project 198 files / 2981 passed / 1 pre-existing platform-gated skip, lint and typecheck exit 0. Confidence is medium rather than high because check rounds run no reachability verifier, so the dismissals below are argued from the code and the passing suite rather than simulated.

business_review.notes: Full acceptance re-audit over the whole branch at 4c21bef found all seven passing; ff130d8 is additive observability and touches none of them.

business_review.item: AC8: lint, typecheck, build and the full test suite pass
business_review.notes: Executed at HEAD ff130d8, not inferred: build exit 0; vitest unit project 198 files / 2981 passed / 1 skipped, exit 0; lint and typecheck exit 0. The prior verdict carried AC8 as partial only because a read-only lens cannot run gates.

business_review.item: Decision 5 (new): never raise a backend entry's auth to a colliding default's
business_review.notes: No rewrite path exists. mergeManagedMcpServers only records; writeDesktopConfig only logs. The orphaned comment that still described the removed floor was fixed in 4c21bef.

business_review.item: Decision 5's binding consequence: the wide and narrow collision tests cannot drift apart
business_review.notes: collidesWithManagedEntry is DEFINED as sameManagedName || sameManagedEndpoint, and the downgrade report keys on sameManagedEndpoint, so a reported downgrade is a strict subset of a displacement by construction. displacedDefaults and keptDefaults are complements of one pass over the same predicate.
Re-audited at 4c21bef. Section 5 and the scope table were amended at Stage 6 to match what shipped.
McpOAuthProvider, mcp-auth.plugin.ts, the SSO origin allowlist, the VS Code connector, mcp-loader.ts and mcp-config.ts untouched; marker state still { managedNames }; bundled defaults file unchanged.

standards_review.notes: 4c21bef and ff130d8 both Conventional Commits, scope proxy, imperative lower-case subject, Refs: EPMCDME-14072 in the body footer. The nine prior commits are untouched — no rebase, no amend.

lint and typecheck exit 0 at HEAD; no `any` in production code; explicit return types on new exports; logging via logger + sanitizeLogArgs. Pre-commit hooks (eslint, vitest, tsc, gitleaks) ran on both commits; --no-verify never used.

Downgraded from partial. The prior rounds' security flag rested on an inaccuracy corrected at Stage 6: the oauth object carries NO secret material — a public clientId, scopes, callback host/port and two endpoint URLs, with no client secret and no token. Getting oauth wrong therefore breaks a connection rather than disclosing anything, which is also what makes Decision 1's pass-through safe. The warn payload is inside sanitizeLogArgs.

finding_status.notes: Adjudicated, not escalated, per the user's explicit instruction to work autonomously. The auth floor is removed (6645e66); spec.md carries it as Decision 5 with the rationale and the rejected alternative. resolveDesktopOAuth is again the single decider of the written value.
Moot by construction. With the floor gone there is no second behavior to disagree; the predicate is decomposed rather than duplicated, so the wide test contains the narrow one.

Adjudicated as pre-existing: parseJsonArray predates the branch and the reconcile path's use of it is unchanged. The asymmetry with selectDefaultsForFailedFetch is intentional — each helper takes the conservative answer to its own question — and there is no recoverable content in a non-array value. Moved to code-review-deferred.md; a code comment at the call site records it.

Round 4. Blind and edge-case convergent: unifying the predicate in round 3 made the downgrade warn fire for a backend entry merely reusing a default's NAME at a different endpoint — the ordinary tenant case, warning on every run. Fixed in 4c21bef by scoping the report to sameManagedEndpoint. Two RED tests pinned it before the fix.
Round 4. Both lenses: the nested loop pushed one record per (default, entry) pair, inflating oauthDowngradeCount. Now at most one record per org entry.
Round 4. Edge-case and acceptance convergent: a comment still promised 'an applied auth floor is visible in the field' after the floor was removed. Reworded.

Round 4, acceptance. The spec scope table understated what shipped — desktop.ts also gained mergeManagedMcpServers, selectDefaultsForFailedFetch, summarizeManagedOauthShapes and parseManagedServerList, and a third test file was edited. spec.md now declares all of it in a second scope table with the review finding that forced each.

Round 4, acceptance. The aliasing test asserted against its own local input array, never against DEFAULT_MANAGED_MCP_SERVERS — the readonly process-lifetime constant §6 exists to protect. A reference-identity assertion against the real constant was added.

Round 4, acceptance. Two downgrade tests asserted oauth is undefined, a shape production never writes because mapCanonicalToDesktop always resolves it. Those fixtures now route through the real mapper and assert false.

Round 5. Blind and edge-case convergent, with edge-case independently proposing the adopted remedy: a displaced OAuth-bearing bundled default was recorded nowhere, so an operator could not tell 'intentionally replaced' from 'silently dropped'. Fixed in ff130d8 by displacedDefaults / displacedDefaultCount on the write-time info record. Three RED tests pinned it.

Round 5, edge-case (medium confidence). Rerouting fixtures through mapCanonicalToDesktop for CR-015 removed the only coverage for an entry whose optional oauth key is omitted entirely — the courier contract. A focused test was restored.

Both round-5 lenses proposed normalizing URL comparison, as the same gap makes a slash-variant same-endpoint downgrade escape the endpoint-scoped report. Rejected for this task: it changes which entries displace which, touches AC5, and contradicts spec §5's stated convention. Already the pre-existing deferred finding; the sidecar now records this second consequence and names the right fix (one normalizing comparison inside sameManagedEndpoint, comparison only). Harm reduced via CR-016 rather than eliminated.

Verified against the source and dropped: the warn payload IS inside sanitizeLogArgs; the downgrade loop iterates the defaults PARAMETER, not the filtered survivors, so it is not dead code; ManagedMcpServerEntry.url is required and mapCanonicalToDesktop drops entries without one, so the url-less comparison is unreachable; the seven bundled defaults have distinct names and URLs, so the two-defaults-one-url and double-match cases cannot arise; a bundled default carries only oauth: true, so an org entry with oauth: true is not a downgrade relative to it and no bundled default can hold a full config to be 'partially' downgraded; the renamed AppliedOauthFloor/appliedOauthFloors surface has no referent outside desktop.ts (grep-verified), so nothing broke silently.
